standard_prerequisites.use: Irreducible components of a fibre, closures of components, and the behaviour of the component count for finite type morphisms; the spreading argument is retained.

core_obligations: Spread the closures of the irreducible components of the generic fibre to a neighbourhood of the generic point.
Show that the spread components remain distinct in every fibre over a nonempty open, giving the lower bound n.

proof_roadmap.step: Decompose the generic fibre into irreducible components.
Spread their closures to a neighbourhood.
Show the components stay distinct in nearby fibres.

difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism over an irreducible base, if the generic fibre has n irreducible components then every fibre over a nonempty open has at least n irreducible components. The proof decomposes the generic fibre into its components, spreads the closures of those components to a neighbourhood using finite type and the irreducibility of the base, and then shows that the spread components remain distinct in each nearby fibre. Keeping the spread components distinct is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 7401-7429.
